pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

GLM-4V training dies at the first attention layer on every transformers version this repo
supports.

`glm4v_attn_forward` replaces `Glm4vTextAttention.forward` whenever `use_remove_padding` or
`ulysses_sp_size > 1` (`monkey_patch.py:473`), so this is the ordinary GLM-4V path, not a corner:

```python
from transformers.models.glm4v.modeling_glm4v import apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb, repeat_kv
```

```
transformers 5.3.0
ImportError: cannot import name 'apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb'
             from 'transformers.models.glm4v.modeling_glm4v'
```

transformers 5.0 replaced `apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb(q, k, cos, sin, mrope_section)` with
`apply_rotary_pos_emb(q, k, cos, sin)` and moved the sectioning into
`Glm4vTextRotaryEmbedding`, which reads `mrope_section` from `config.rope_parameters` and folds
it into cos/sin before the attention ever sees them. `Glm4vTextAttention.forward` upstream is
now just:

```python
cos, sin = position_embeddings
query_states, key_states = apply_rotary_pos_emb(query_states, key_states, cos, sin)
```

Absent in every supported version — `requirements.txt` asks for
`transformers>=5.5.3,!=5.6.0,<5.11`, and the extras pin 5.3.0 / 5.5.3:

| transformers | `apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb` in `modeling_glm4v` |
| --- | --- |
| 4.57.1 | yes |
| 5.0.0, 5.3.0, 5.5.3, 5.10.4, 5.16.1 | no |

It came in with #5724 (`transformers upgrade to 5.3.0`), which updated the config-side
`rope_scaling` → `rope_parameters` migration a few lines above but not the function that moved
with it.

`qwen2_vl.py` uses the same call and is **not** affected: `modeling_qwen2_vl` still exports
`apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb`. Only GLM-4V was migrated.

### The change

Call the function upstream calls, and drop the `mrope_section` lookup that fed the old one.

That lookup was dead twice over — it reads `self.rope_scaling` or `self.rope_parameter` off the
**attention module**, and on transformers 5 the attention module has neither (the config
attribute is `rope_parameters`, plural, and lives on the config):

```
transformers 5.3.0, Glm4vTextAttention
  self.rope_scaling    -> <ABSENT>
  self.rope_parameter  -> <ABSENT>
```

so the `assert` under it would have fired had the import ever got that far.

Restoring the old function instead would be wrong, not just unavailable: the 4.x call expects
cos/sin with a leading 3-section dim, and applying it to what transformers 5 produces raises
`IndexError: index 1 is out of bounds for dimension 0 with size 1`. The sectioning genuinely
moved.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. No PR or issue mentions `apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb` on this
      repo; the one hit, #2603, predates the 5.x upgrade and is closed.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

`tests/models/test_glm4v_rotary_on_cpu.py`, following the `on_cpu.py` convention so it runs in
`cpu_unit_tests.yml`. It builds a real `Glm4vTextAttention` and `Glm4vTextRotaryEmbedding`, runs
`glm4v_attn_forward` with the CUDA-only flash-attention call patched out, and asserts the q/k
reaching attention equal `apply_rotary_pos_emb(q, k, cos, sin)` — the same rotary upstream
applies — with KV repeated to the query head count. A second case records why the argument had
to go rather than be restored.

Load-bearing, run against a clean `origin/main` worktree in the same environment:

```
$ pytest tests/models/test_glm4v_rotary_on_cpu.py          # origin/main
>       from transformers.models.glm4v.modeling_glm4v import apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb, repeat_kv
E       ImportError: cannot import name 'apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb' ...
1 failed, 1 passed

$ pytest tests/models/test_glm4v_rotary_on_cpu.py          # this branch
2 passed

$ ruff check / ruff format --check                          # ruff 0.12.2, as pinned in .pre-commit-config.yaml
All checks passed! / 2 files already formatted

$ python3 tests/special_sanity/check_license.py --directories .
exit 0
```

The flash-attention call itself is CUDA-only and unchanged by this PR, so it stays covered by
the existing GPU tests.

### API and Usage Example

No API change.

### Design & Code Changes

One import and one call site in `verl/models/transformers/glm4v.py`; the `mrope_section`
derivation is removed with them.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting).
- [x] Add / update the documentation. Not applicable.
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s).
pull_request.title: [model] fix: use the transformers 5 rotary API in the GLM-4V attention patch
pull_request.head: fix/glm4v-rotary-transformers-5
pull_request.diff:
@@ -288,7 +288,7 @@ def glm4v_attn_forward(
     position_embeddings: Optional[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]] = None,  # will become mandatory in v4.46
     **kwargs,
 ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, None, None]:
-    from transformers.models.glm4v.modeling_glm4v import apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb, repeat_kv
+    from transformers.models.glm4v.modeling_glm4v import apply_rotary_pos_emb, repeat_kv
 
     bsz, q_len, _ = hidden_states.size()  # q_len = seq_length / sp_size
     query_states = self.q_proj(hidden_states)  # (batch_size, seq_length / sp_size, num_heads * head_size)
@@ -300,17 +300,10 @@ def glm4v_attn_forward(
     value_states = value_states.view(bsz, q_len, self.num_key_value_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
 
     # Because the input can be padded, the absolute sequence length depends on the max position id.
+    # Glm4vTextRotaryEmbedding already folds mrope_section into cos/sin, so this is the plain
+    # application, exactly as Glm4vTextAttention.forward does it.
     cos, sin = position_embeddings
-    if getattr(self, "rope_scaling", None) is not None:
-        # for transformers < 5.0.0
-        mrope_section = self.rope_scaling.get("mrope_section", None)
-    else:
-        # for transformers >= 5.0.0, only rope_parameters present in the config
-        assert getattr(self, "rope_parameter", None) is not None, (
-            "Either rope_scaling or rope_parameter should be defined in the config for GLM4V."
-        )
-        mrope_section = self.rope_parameter.get("mrope_section", None)
-    query_states, key_states = apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb(query_states, key_states, cos, sin, mrope_section)
+    query_states, key_states = apply_rotary_pos_emb(query_states, key_states, cos, sin)
     key_states = repeat_kv(key_states, self.num_key_value_groups)
     value_states = repeat_kv(value_states, self.num_key_value_groups)
     dropout_rate = 0.0 if not self.training else self.attention_dropout

comments.body: Removed. The import and rotary-call fix in `glm4v.py` stands on its own — `apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb` does not exist in any transformers this repo supports, so the GLM-4V path raises ImportError at the first attention layer with remove_padding or ulysses_sp_size > 1.

comments.body:
The `vllm` / `vllm_ascend` reds here are not from this PR — it touches one file,
`verl/models/transformers/glm4v.py`, and neither job exercises it.

```
tests/workers/rollout/rollout_vllm/test_vllm_abort.py::test_abort_all_requests_propagates_pause_failure
    AttributeError: 'vLLMHttpServer' object has no attribute '_resume_event'
    verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py:942
```

That test builds the server with `vLLMHttpServer.__new__(vLLMHttpServer)`, so `__init__` never
runs and neither `_submission_paused` nor `_resume_event` is set. `abort_all_requests` started
touching both in #7511 ("gate rollout submission during weight-sync drain for DP>1"), which
lands before the `pause_generation` call the test is actually asserting on. The test file has
not been updated since.

Happy to send that as a separate one-liner if it is not already being handled.
